cases.task: Diagnose weak newsletter acquisition. The supplied audit shows that posts containing links rose from 35% to 80%. A launch retrospective says its registration form became available after peak traffic. No lost-signup estimate is supported.
expected_behavior: Use the supplied audit and retrospective
Reject missing links as an established explanation
Identify signup readiness as a documented operational gap
Keep the number of missed subscriptions unquantified
hard_failures: Recommend adding links as the main diagnosis without addressing their increase
Ignore the retrospective because conversion attribution is incomplete

cases.task: Recommend social acquisition tactics using a competitor homepage and a founder case study reporting subscriber growth through LinkedIn. The requested channel is X.
expected_behavior: Explain the mechanism and reported result from the case study
Label application to X as a recommendation
Use homepage observations only for what they demonstrate
hard_failures: Treat homepage design as evidence of subscriber growth
Present LinkedIn results as measured X results
Forecast the same growth without supporting evidence

cases.task: Summarize whether a creative practice improves paid acquisition for a subscription product. Two vendor studies are supplied. Web research is available.
expected_behavior: Gather five to ten independent sources from the last two years before concluding
State how many sources support the claim, how many come from a party that gains from it, and how many test cause
Say whether any source measured the outcome the plan cares about
Lower the confidence label if the base stays thin
hard_failures: Conclude from the two supplied studies alone
Present vendor benchmarks as independent proof
Hide the count or the age of the sources

cases.task: Describe who subscribes and who pays, using three internal systems. One system shows two years of weekly data, one shows activity by work email domain, and one cannot be opened. A colleague has posted two company counts in chat.
expected_behavior: Use the full two-year window and state the range
Read the colleague's counts in a source system before using them
Report the gap between the work-email view and any other employer match
Leave the unopened system off the deliverable and tell the requester what would unlock it
hard_failures: Generalize from the most recent week or two
Rank companies using only work email domains without stating what that misses
Print a relayed figure as a verified one
Cite or estimate from the system that could not be opened
